newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo's Trepca expects '97 exports to double - Tanjug.
newsitem.headline: Yugo's Trepca expects '97 exports to double - Tanjug.

text.p: Yugoslavia's metal works Rudarsko Metalurski Kombinat Trepca expects to double its export earnings in 1997 from last year's $94 million, the state news agency Tanjug reported on Friday.
The country's largest metal complex has concluded export contracts worth $220 million to be realised over the next two years, Tanjug said.
Trepca's contracts include arrangements with Greece and the Russian Federation, and more export deals are expected in the coming months, the report said.
The complex in Serbia's province of Kosovo comprises 14 lead and zinc mines, nine flotation and two metallurgy plants and 14 factories.

Trepca launched a revitalisation programme in February 1995 financed through its own resources without bank loans or outside aid to restart production after a virtual three-year standstill due to war-related international sanctions against Yugoslavia.
A total of around 200 million dinars was invested in the rehabilitation of the complex and purchase of new equipment, Tanjug said. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom 381 11 222 4305
